competitors.title: Picking a Durable Workflow Engine for AI Agents in 2026
key_points: Deep architectural split: replay-based (Temporal, Restate, Hatchet) vs checkpoint-based (Trigger.dev v4, LangGraph)
Replay: workflow code must be deterministic; platform records event history and replays on recovery — gives free audit trail and time-travel debugging
Checkpoint: workflow code can be non-deterministic; platform snapshots state at await points — no determinism requirement, no full event-history audit trail
Inngest sits orthogonally: event-driven step functions, each step is a durable atomic unit retried automatically
Agent workloads are non-deterministic by construction — LLM calls return different text every run; replay-based platforms require wrapping every LLM call in a deterministic activity
Temporal payload-codec footnote: LLM payloads large; per-event blob limit 2MB, per-workflow history 50MB; claim-check pattern with S3 is the standard workaround
Decision framework: regulated legal-AI agent → Temporal; early-stage research agent → Trigger.dev; event-driven triage → Inngest; open-source self-host → Restate
